IX 
 
 
Acknowledgements 
 
 
The edition of the Mahāvastu presented in this volume was prepared at the International 
Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (IRIAB) at Soka University, Japan, where I have 
been staying as a recipient of the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS) 
Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (October/2018 -; 18F18005). This work could 
not have been completed had it not been for the generous financial support of the Fellowship, 
which enabled me to fully concentrate on my project. I would like to express my deepest 
gratitude to the JSPS for this great opportunity.  
 
I would like to express my sincere thanks to Prof. Oskar von Hinüber, who kindly agreed 
to help me with some difficult sections of the text, despite being very busy with his own projects. 
Had it not been for his corrections and valuable suggestions, many of the vague readings would 
have been unresolved. 
 
I am grateful to the staff of the IRIAB, Prof. Noriyuki Kudo, for their help and checking 
the final draft of this publication. 
 
I am thankful to Prof. Marek Me jor for his continuous guidance and support  during all 
my academic endeavours. 
 
I would like to thank Susan Roach for checking the English of this publication and 
offering many suggestions and corrections. 
 
There are quite a few forms and longer passages i n this volume, which I was not able to 
understand or correct satisfactorily. I hope that more detailed research on particular chapters 
will be conducted in the future and that this will result in better readings. 
 
 
 
Katarzyna Marciniak 
Hachioji,  March 2020

Signs 
 
< > omitted part(s) of the text without a gap in the manuscript  
← α ← β: the form β should be changed to α 
α < β the form α comes from β 
α ∈ β α is a scribal error, a corruption, or a hyper-form of β 
α ≠ β β does not agree with α 
*… a hypothetical form which is not attested anywhere, e.g. *snāru 
…* virāma 
.. one lost (or illegible) akṣara 
° except for letters, following or preceding the sign, the word is the same as the  
 preceding one 
≠ mss.  “against the mss.”; applied to Senart’s emendations made against the readings in  the mss.

1 Sa Na nigalitā (s.e.); Sen. niriṃgitā; *niliṅgita in the meaning of āliṅgita “encircled, embraced”?; I keep this 
reading but it is doubtful. In the two verses which follow the mss. read niliṃgitā, while in the previous verse the 
reading is viliṃbita (s.e. for vilaṃbitā?); the parallel verse in Mv(KM) 3.354f. reads naliṅgitā, which is also 
obscure. However, vilaṃbita “hanging” would be acceptable only in the verses concerning jewellery and gems, 
but it cannot be correct in the one concerning satvadhātu. Cf. the readings a few lines above: yena bodhiṃ tato 
gatāḥ; sarve tatomukhā abhū; and in Mv(KM) 3.356 sarve tatomukhā āsi yena bodhi maharṣiṇo.

6 Sen. me edṛśo.   7 Corr. Na; Sa so.   8 Corr. Sen.; Sa Na dṛṣṭvā.   
9 Sen. Śakreṇa devānām indreṇa. 
10 Corr. Na; Sa dāntaṃ. 
11 Sen. bhonti. 
12 Sa Na samāgamo; Sen. samāgataḥ. 
13 Śloka; pāda a is hypermetrical; in pāda b we should read bhonti for bhavanti m.c.; pāda c becomes a regular 
Pathyā if we read bhāryā (instr. fem. -ā) for bhāryāya. Cf. Mv(KM) 3.34 evaṃ puṇyavato arthā sarve bhonti 
pradakṣiṇā ǀ yathā nāma Kuśo bhartā jñātīhi ca samāgato ǀǀ. 
14 Sa rājñā jyojyeṣṭho (s.e.); Na Sen. rājñāṃ yo jyeṣṭho. 
15 Corr. Sen.; Sa Na anyo.
